title: Epigenetic pathways linking prenatal alcohol exposure to fetal alcohol spectrum disorder
title_zh: 将产前酒精暴露与胎儿酒精谱系障碍联系起来的表观遗传通路
abstract: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) presents a profound global health burden, yet clinical diagnosis remains severely hindered by phenotypic heterogeneity and the lack of objective biomarkers. Emerging evidence reveals that the pathogenesis of prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) is heavily driven by fetal programming via epigenetic modifications. In this narrative review, we synthesize data from human cohorts and advanced preclinical models to conceptualize FASD as a dynamic epigenetic trajectory rather than a static teratogenic insult. Ethanol disrupts the epigenome systemically, perturbing one-carbon metabolism, oxidative stress pathways, non-coding RNAs, and the placenta-brain axis. Furthermore, postnatal environmental factors, particularly early-life stress, interact with PAE to shape neuroimmune vulnerability and sexually dimorphic outcomes. While stable peripheral DNA methylation "episignatures" offer significant promise for future risk stratification, we highlight the critical translational challenge of correlating these peripheral markers with central neuropathology. Although AI-assisted screening and targeted epigenetic interventions (e.g., choline supplementation) represent exciting translational avenues, they remain investigational. Ultimately, transitioning FASD toward precision medicine will require longitudinal, single-cell multi-omic studies to validate tissue-specific biomarkers, address ethical and algorithmic biases, and pave the way for biologically grounded, early interventions.
abstract_zh: 胎儿酒精谱系障碍（FASD）构成严重的全球健康负担，但因表型异质性和缺乏客观生物标志物，临床诊断仍受限。新兴证据表明，产前酒精暴露（PAE）的发病机制在很大程度上由通过表观遗传修饰介导的胎儿编程驱动。在这篇叙述性综述中，我们整合了人群队列和先进前临床模型的数据，将FASD概念化为一种动态表观遗传轨迹，而非静态致畸损伤。酒精系统性干扰表观基因组，扰动一碳代谢、氧化应激通路、非编码RNA及胎盘—脑轴。此外，产后环境因素，尤其是早期生活压力，与PAE交互，塑造神经免疫易感性和性二形态差异结局。尽管稳定的外周DNA甲基化“表观签名”在未来风险分层上前景显著，我们强调其与中枢神经病理相关联的关键转化挑战。尽管AI辅助筛查与靶向表观遗传干预（如胆碱补充）代表了令人期待的转化方向，但仍处于探索阶段。最终，将FASD推向精准医学需依赖纵向单细胞多组学研究，以验证组织特异性生物标志物，解决伦理与算法偏倚问题，并推动生物学基础更坚实、早期的干预策略。
